title: Nitter repository unarchived, development to continue
content:
A new commit has been pushed to the open‑source “Nitter” project, a privacy‑focused front‑end for Twitter, under the repository zedeus/nitter. Identified by the hash 1428b4c2b4246f92a7e5b2673438e5fb39fcc4a3, the change updates the application’s handling of media URLs and refines the rate‑limiting logic that governs API requests. The modifications also include a minor dependency upgrade to address a known security advisory, and they adjust default configuration values to improve stability on low‑resource deployments.

The update was posted on GitHub and quickly surfaced on Hacker News, where the submission received 15 points despite attracting no comments. The brief community reaction suggests that the change is being noted by users who rely on Nitter for an ad‑free, non‑tracking Twitter experience, while the lack of discussion indicates the patch is viewed as a routine maintenance improvement rather than a controversial alteration.
author: Hacker News

title: Nitter project continues after legal advice
content:
A GitHub repository for Nitter, an open‑source, privacy‑focused front‑end for Twitter, has attracted notable attention on the technology news site Hacker News. The project, maintained at github.com/zedeus/nitter, offers users a lightweight interface that strips tracking scripts and presents tweets without requiring a Twitter account. On the Hacker News discussion page (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49589003), the post garnered 147 points and generated 27 comments, indicating strong community interest in alternatives that enhance user privacy and reduce reliance on the official Twitter platform.

The discussion highlighted Nitter’s ability to serve as a proxy that caches media, supports RSS feeds, and can be self‑hosted, making it appealing for both casual users and developers seeking to embed Twitter content without exposing personal data. Contributors noted recent updates to the codebase, improved compatibility with Twitter’s API changes, and growing adoption across various instances. The conversation reflects broader trends toward decentralized web services and the demand for tools that mitigate data collection by major social networks.
author: Hacker News

title: AfD leads Saxony-Anhalt state election as polls close
content:
“Everything is possible,” the slogan of the far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD), echoed across polling stations as Saxony‑Anhalt voters cast their ballots in the state election that concluded today. The phrase, promoted by the party’s leading candidate Ulrich Siegmund, frames the contest as a pivotal moment for Germany’s political landscape, with the AfD seeking to translate its surge in public support into executive power for the first time in the state.

Siegmund, who has consistently topped opinion polls ahead of the vote, stands poised to become Saxony‑Anhalt’s next Minister‑President if the party’s share of the vote translates into a governing majority or a viable coalition partner. The AfD’s ascendancy in the eastern state reflects broader shifts in voter sentiment, as concerns over immigration, economic restructuring and national identity have bolstered the party’s appeal since its entry into the Bundestag in 2017. Election officials will now begin the count, and the final results are expected to be announced within the next 24 hours, setting the stage for coalition talks that will determine whether the AfD can convert its campaign momentum into governmental authority.
author: France 24

title: Palestinian farmers in Hebron confront settler sabotage and military restrictions
content:
West Bank farmers have continued to work their fields despite a series of daily challenges that include settler attacks, the theft of livestock and restrictions imposed by the Israeli military. According to reports from local agricultural cooperatives, the farms are located in areas near major settlement blocs where clashes between Palestinian residents and Israeli settlers are frequent. Farmers say they regularly face harassment from settlers who attempt to damage crops and fence off portions of the land, while incidents of sheep and goat theft have risen sharply over the past year. Military regulations further complicate agricultural activities, as access to certain fields requires permits that are often delayed or denied, and roadblocks limit the transport of produce to markets.

The persistence of the farmers has been documented by several humanitarian organizations, which note that the community relies on the land for both livelihood and cultural identity. Despite the obstacles, the growers employ traditional irrigation methods and coordinate with neighboring villages to share resources and security information. Officials from the Israeli Defense Forces have stated that they are investigating settler violence, while Palestinian authorities have called for greater protection of agricultural zones. The continued cultivation of the disputed territories underscores the resilience of the West Bank’s farming population amid ongoing tensions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix after starting 19th
content:
Italian driver Luca Antonelli delivered a dramatic performance at the Monza Grand Prix on Sunday, climbing from 19th on the grid to claim victory in a race that secured him the season‑long championship. The win marked the first time in six decades that an Italian has captured the title in the series, ending a 60‑year drought for the nation’s motorsport fans.

Antonelli’s surge began on the opening lap, where he overtook several competitors before the first chicane. By the midway point he had moved into the top five, and a decisive pit‑stop strategy allowed him to undercut the race leader on lap 34. He maintained a consistent pace through the high‑speed straights of the Autodromo Nazionale, ultimately crossing the finish line ahead of his closest rival by 0.8 seconds. The victory awarded him 25 points, bringing his total to 212, which placed him eight points clear of the runner‑up with two races remaining in the calendar.

The championship triumph not only highlights Antonelli’s rapid development as a driver but also revives Italy’s presence at the pinnacle of the sport. Team officials praised his composure under pressure, while the win is expected to boost interest in the series across the country ahead of the season’s final events.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN launches $50 million appeal for Nepal flood survivors as death toll tops 1,300
content:
The United Nations has launched a $50 million humanitarian appeal to assist more than 84,000 people displaced by recent monsoon floods in Nepal. The appeal, announced by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), comes as flood‑affected communities face heightened risk of cholera and severe sanitation shortfalls, prompting urgent calls for resources to prevent a public‑health emergency.

The funding is earmarked for emergency water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions, cholera surveillance, medical treatment, temporary shelter and food distribution, as well as support for the Nepalese government’s recovery plans. UN agencies, together with international partners, will coordinate the delivery of services and infrastructure repairs, aiming to restore safe water access and reduce disease transmission while stabilising livelihoods. The appeal seeks contributions from donor nations and private entities to meet the immediate needs and to lay the groundwork for longer‑term resilience in the flood‑hit regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 to keep perfect Premier League start
content:
Arsenal secured a hard‑won victory in what manager Mikel Arteta described as the “stiffest test” of their Premier League title defence to date, overturning a first‑half deficit to claim three points. The Gunners fell behind early in the match but responded with a surge of attacking play, equalising through a well‑timed header before netting the winner from a swift counter‑attack in the second half. The result extended Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table and marked their first successful comeback of the season.

The win comes as Arsenal seek to consolidate their position ahead of a congested fixture schedule, having maintained an unbeaten run in the league since the start of the campaign. By navigating this challenging encounter, the team demonstrated resilience and depth, qualities that will be crucial as they aim to retain the Premier League crown. The victory also reinforces their standing ahead of upcoming domestic and European commitments, keeping them firmly in contention for the title.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 10-year-old Algerian boy dies after four days trapped in well
content:
Rescuers in Algeria have recovered the body of 10‑year‑old Ayoub, who died after becoming trapped in a well earlier this week. The incident, which occurred in the rural outskirts of the Tamanrasset province, prompted an immediate response from local emergency services and volunteers who worked through the night to locate the child.

Authorities said that a coordinated effort involving the national civil protection agency, fire brigade units and community members was launched within hours of the well‑fall. Divers and specialized equipment were deployed to widen the shaft and retrieve the boy, but despite the rapid response, Ayoub did not survive. Officials confirmed that the well had no protective covering and warned that similar unguarded structures pose a serious risk in remote areas. An investigation into the circumstances of the accident has been opened, and local officials urged residents to secure hazardous sites to prevent future tragedies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Aryna Sabalenka reaches US Open quarterfinals
content:
Aryna Sabalenka, the two‑time defending champion, secured her place in the US Open quarterfinals on Tuesday after defeating American qualifier Taylor Townsend in straight sets, 6‑4, 6‑3. The match, played on Court 17 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, marked Sabalenka’s fifth consecutive appearance in the tournament’s last eight.

Sabalenka’s victory came after a solid first‑set performance in which she broke Townsend’s serve twice before consolidating the lead. In the second set, she maintained pressure with aggressive baseline play and a high first‑serve percentage, limiting Townsend’s opportunities to mount a comeback. The win extends Sabalenka’s unbeaten run at the US Open to 13 matches, positioning her for a potential third straight title as she prepares for a quarterfinal clash against the winner of the parallel match between [opponent’s name] and [opponent’s name].
author: Al Jazeera

title: Witkoff says Ukraine peace talks are very meaningful
content:
Ukrainian‑American diplomat Michael Witkoff told reporters on Thursday that the latest round of peace negotiations concerning the conflict in Ukraine has been “very meaningful.” Speaking after a three‑day session in Geneva that brought together representatives from Kyiv, Moscow and a coalition of European mediators, Witkoff said the talks produced a set of actionable proposals on cease‑fire monitoring, humanitarian corridors and the phased withdrawal of foreign forces.

The participants reviewed progress on previously agreed security guarantees and examined mechanisms for the return of displaced civilians, while also addressing the status of contested territories. Witkoff noted that both sides expressed a willingness to move forward on the outlined steps, though final ratification will require further diplomatic engagement. Observers indicated that the dialogue marks a notable shift from earlier stalemates, and the international community will continue to support the process as it advances toward a formal settlement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Argentina renews claim to Falkland Islands 44 years after war
content:
More than four decades after the 1982 conflict that pitted the United Kingdom against Argentina over the Falkland Islands, the Argentine government has formally renewed its claim to the archipelago. In a statement released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday, President Javier Milei reaffirmed Argentina’s “historical, legal and moral right” to the islands, known locally as Islas Malvinas, and announced that Buenos Aires will seek renewed discussion of the sovereignty issue at forthcoming United Nations forums. The declaration follows a series of diplomatic moves, including the appointment of a senior envoy to coordinate a multilateral campaign and the preparation of a legal brief to be submitted to the International Court of Justice, although the court’s jurisdiction would require the consent of both parties.

The United Kingdom, which has administered the Falklands continuously since the war’s end, reiterated its position that the islands’ status will not be altered without the explicit consent of the islanders, a stance supported by a 2013 referendum in which 99.8 % voted to remain a British Overseas Territory. While the renewed Argentine push has been welcomed by some Latin American governments, it has not yet led to any substantive change in the diplomatic relationship between London and Buenos Aires. Observers note that the latest assertion is part of a broader pattern of Argentine efforts to keep the sovereignty question on the international agenda, but the dispute remains unresolved as both nations maintain their respective claims.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran threatens stronger response after U.S. strikes on its oil tankers
content:
Washington announced on Monday that U.S. forces had struck Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for a series of attacks by Tehran on U.S. warships operating in the region. The strikes targeted vessels believed to be transporting fuel for the Iranian navy and were described by the Pentagon as a proportional response aimed at deterring further aggression against American naval assets. The attacks on the warships, which occurred earlier in the week, involved missile fire and small‑boat assaults that caused minor damage but prompted a swift escalation in the ongoing maritime tension between the two nations.

The remarks from U.S. officials came a day after the naval engagement, underscoring Washington’s intent to maintain freedom of navigation and protect its forces in the contested waters. Both sides have exchanged accusations, with Tehran condemning the U.S. action as an unlawful act of war, while the United States reaffirmed its right to defend its vessels. The situation remains volatile, and officials indicated that further diplomatic and military measures will be considered as events develop.
author: BBC World

title: Stoke Space and Relativity Space Advance LC-14 and LC-16 Toward First Flights
content:
Along Missile Row at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, two private launch providers are moving their new launch complexes closer to operational status. Stoke Space is preparing Launch Complex‑14 (LC‑14) for the first flight of its small‑satellite rocket, while Relativity Space is advancing Launch Complex‑16 (LC‑16) toward the maiden launch of its 3‑stage R‑Star vehicle. Both sites are situated on the historic Missile Row corridor, a stretch of Cape infrastructure that has supported U.S. spaceflight since the 1950s.

Stoke Space’s LC‑14 is a compact, reusable pad designed to accommodate its 4‑tonne “Stoke‑1” vehicle. The company has completed pad construction and is conducting static‑fire tests of the rocket’s Merlin‑derived engines. Relativity Space, meanwhile, is finalizing the 3‑stage R‑Star’s 3‑D‑printed aluminum‑lithium alloy airframe and installing the launch‑pad support infrastructure at LC‑16. Both companies have announced target launch windows for late 2026, with each company’s first flight expected to demonstrate the viability of their respective propulsion and manufacturing approaches.

With LC‑14 and LC‑16 approaching readiness, the Cape’s launch portfolio will expand to include two additional commercial launch sites that emphasize rapid development and cost efficiency. The successful first flights of Stoke‑1 and R‑Star would provide new options for small‑satellite operators and further diversify the commercial launch market at Cape Canaveral.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Top 10 Lego Star Wars Starships to Own
content:
**Lego Unveils Ten New Star Wars Starship Sets for Fans of All Allegiances**

Lego has announced a new line of ten Star Wars starship sets that promise to satisfy both Jedi and Sith enthusiasts alike. The collection, released in March 2026, includes iconic vessels such as the X‑Wing, TIE Fighter, Millennium Falcon, Imperial Star Destroyer, Slave I, AT‑AT, Y‑Wing, TIE Interceptor, Super Star Destroyer, and the Death Star. Each set features between 1,200 and 4,500 pieces, with release prices ranging from $59.99 for the TIE Fighter to $299.99 for the Death Star. The sets also incorporate interactive elements—such as moving wings, rotating turrets, and sound modules—designed to replicate the action-packed moments seen in the films.

The new line arrives as part of Lego’s ongoing partnership with Lucasfilm, which has expanded the franchise’s presence in the toy market since 2015. The sets are available in both retail stores and online, with limited-edition variants offering exclusive stickers and special packaging for collectors. Lego’s marketing team highlighted the sets’ compatibility with existing Star Wars Lego themes, allowing builders to integrate them into larger dioramas or combine them with the recently released “Star Wars: The Mandalorian” and “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker” sets. The release is expected to boost sales in the holiday season, with analysts projecting a 12% increase in Lego’s Star Wars segment revenue.

Industry observers note that the breadth of ships—ranging from the nimble X‑Wing to the massive Death Star—provides a comprehensive representation of the Star Wars universe’s most celebrated spacecraft. The sets’ detailed designs, coupled with their playability, aim to appeal to both seasoned collectors and new fans. As Lego continues to expand its Star Wars catalog, the introduction of these ten starships marks a significant milestone in the brand’s effort to keep the galaxy far, far away alive for the next generation of builders.
author: Space.com

title: SpaceX Launches 27 Starlink Satellites, Falcon 9 Lands on Ship
content:
SpaceX launched a new batch of its Starlink internet satellites on September 6 from a launch site on California’s central coast. The company used its Falcon 9 rocket to lift the payload into orbit, continuing its rapid deployment of the constellation that aims to provide global broadband coverage.

The launch carried a typical payload of dozens of small satellites, each equipped with phased‑array antennas and high‑throughput transponders. The Falcon 9 first stage performed a successful return to the launch site, while the second stage deployed the satellites into a low‑Earth orbit. This mission follows a series of recent launches that have steadily increased the number of operational Starlink satellites worldwide.

With each launch, SpaceX expands the reach of its satellite network, bringing the company closer to its goal of delivering high‑speed internet to underserved regions. The September 6 flight adds to the growing constellation that is already in service in many parts of the globe.
author: Space.com

title: US Navy Launches First V-2 Rocket from Carrier on Sept. 6, 1947
content:
On September 6, 1947, the U.S. Navy successfully launched a V‑2 rocket from the deck of the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise, marking the first time a ballistic missile had been fired from a naval vessel. The test, conducted off the coast of California, demonstrated that a carrier could serve as a mobile launch platform, a capability that would later be leveraged for both military deterrence and space exploration.

The demonstration proved that the Navy could project missile power at sea, reducing the need for fixed launch sites and increasing operational flexibility. It also provided valuable data on the stresses of carrier deck operations, guidance systems, and recovery procedures, informing subsequent missile programs such as the Polaris submarine-launched ballistic missile and the Navy’s early space launch efforts. By showing that a ship could reliably launch a V‑2, the Navy opened a new dimension in strategic planning during the early Cold War.

This event laid groundwork for the development of sea‑based launch vehicles that would become integral to both defense and civilian space programs. It underscored the importance of mobility and rapid deployment in missile technology, influencing U.S. naval strategy and contributing to the eventual establishment of the U.S. space launch infrastructure that would later support the Apollo missions and beyond.
author: Space.com

title: Armstrong Misses Winning Chance as Birmingham and Wolves Draw
content:
Birmingham City secured a 1‑0 victory over Wolverhampton Wanderers at the Molineux Stadium, keeping the Blues unbeaten in the Championship and moving them to second place in the table. The win was largely defined by a single moment of defensive error from Wolves, as Jackson Tchatchoua inadvertently scored an own goal in the first half, sending the ball into the corner that the Wolves striker Adam Armstrong had been targeting in the 87th minute. Had Armstrong found the same corner, the match could have ended in a draw, but the goal proved decisive.

The match was dominated by Birmingham’s disciplined defence and efficient counter‑attacks. After the own goal, Wolves pressed for a quick equaliser, but their attempts were thwarted by a solid backline and a well‑positioned goalkeeper. In the 70th minute, Fer López supplied a precise pass to Birmingham striker César Peixoto, who calmly slotted the ball past the Wolves keeper to extend the Blues’ lead. Despite a late surge from Wolves, the defence held firm, and the team’s unbeaten run in the league continued.

With the victory, Birmingham City solidified their position in the upper half of the Championship standings, while Wolverhampton Wanderers will look to regroup after a disappointing home defeat. The result underscores Birmingham’s resilience and tactical discipline, qualities that will be crucial as the season progresses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maitland‑Niles' 25‑yard goal secures Everton's point against Manchester United
content:
Everton’s search for a new right‑back ended on Monday with the £4.3 million signing of Ainsley Maitland‑Niles, a move that drew mixed reactions from fans and pundits alike. The former Arsenal midfielder, who had been on the fringes of the Premier League, was immediately thrust into the starting lineup for David Moyes’s side as they faced Manchester United at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The decision to start the 24‑year‑old in a high‑stakes fixture underscored the club’s urgency to fill the defensive gap left by the departure of their previous right‑back.

In his debut, Maitland‑Niles delivered a match‑deciding performance. Seventeen minutes into the game, he struck a 25‑yard free‑kick into the top corner of the net, giving Everton a 1‑0 lead that would prove decisive. United had been on the brink of victory after Benjamin Sesko’s 88th‑minute header, but the goal forced a frantic scramble. Everton’s defense held firm for the remainder of the match, and the win preserved their unbeaten start to the season, a point that was all the more valuable given the turmoil of the transfer deadline day.

The result has reinforced Everton’s resolve to remain competitive in the Premier League. With a fresh right‑back now contributing immediately, the club’s defensive stability is expected to improve, while the victory over a title‑contender has bolstered confidence ahead of a challenging fixture list. The match also highlighted the importance of decisive moments in tight games, as Maitland‑Niles’ goal proved pivotal in securing a point against a formidable opponent.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Antonelli Wins Italian GP, Ending 60-Year Wait
content:
Kimi Antonelli claimed his first Formula 1 victory at the Italian Grand Prix, turning a 19th‑grid start into a historic win at Monza. The 22‑year‑old Mercedes driver out‑paced his teammate George Russell, who had begun the race from second and finished second. Antonelli’s late‑race surge, combined with a strong performance from Max Verstappen, who secured third place for Red Bull, underscored a dramatic day for the championship contenders.

Lewis Hamilton finished sixth in the race, while Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc avoided serious injury after a high‑speed crash at the Parabolica corner early in the event. Leclerc’s exit from the track was a relief for the team, as the incident could have jeopardised his season. The race also saw a mix of strategic pit stops and tire choices, with Mercedes and Red Bull capitalising on their cars’ reliability and the drivers’ skill to secure the top three positions.

The Italian Grand Prix highlighted the unpredictable nature of Formula 1, where a driver starting from the back of the grid can still claim victory. Antonelli’s triumph at his home circuit added a memorable chapter to the season, while the performances of Russell, Verstappen, Hamilton, and Leclerc set the stage for the remaining races in the championship.
author: Guardian Sport

title: US Open 2026 Fourth Round: Sabalenka Faces Townsend at Flushing Meadows
content:
Fourth‑round action at Flushing Meadows saw a tense doubles match that ended 4‑4, with the pair facing a decisive tie‑break against the reigning champion. Daniel, who has been following the tournament closely, shared updates on his social‑media channels, encouraging fans to keep up on TikTok and Bluesky for live commentary. The match featured a strategic battle between Townsend and Sabalenka, with Townsend employing topspin cross‑cushion shots aimed at Sabalenka’s backhand to force her outside the lines. Townsend also attempted to slow the pace, hoping to frustrate the champion who typically dislikes prolonged wind‑ups.

In addition to the on‑court drama, Townsend’s appearance drew attention when he wore a coat reminiscent of the Night’s Watch, a detail that sparked commentary among spectators and commentators alike. Analysts noted that the wind‑swept conditions at the venue may have influenced the players’ tactics, with Townsend’s slower play potentially capitalizing on the unpredictable breeze. The match concluded with a tightly contested finish, leaving fans eager to see how the remaining rounds will unfold.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maro Itoje Recalled to England Squad
content:
England’s second‑row forward Maro Itoje has re‑joined the national squad after being named in the 36‑man training group for the autumn Nations Championship. The 28‑year‑old, who has been a key player for the Wasps and the national team, was added to the extended squad as the side prepares for its upcoming test matches against the home nations and France.

Itoje’s inclusion follows a period of injury‑related absences that saw him miss earlier fixtures. The England coaching staff have highlighted his experience and work rate as valuable assets for the team’s forward pack, and his return to the set‑up is expected to bolster the squad’s depth ahead of the high‑profile autumn series. The training squad will continue to refine strategies and assess player fitness in the lead‑up to the first match of the Championship.
author: BBC Sport

title: England beat Ireland 3-0, Dunkley scores century
content:
England’s women’s cricket team capped their international summer with a decisive victory over Ireland at Worcester, winning by 114 runs. Sophia Dunkley led the attack, scoring a brilliant 119 runs to steer England to a comfortable total, while the Irish bowlers struggled to contain the English side.

The match, played on a day that offered little assistance to the bowlers, saw England post a formidable score before their bowlers dismantled Ireland’s batting lineup. Ireland were bowled out for a modest total, and England’s bowlers exploited the conditions to secure a comprehensive win. The result confirms England’s dominance in the current international circuit and leaves Ireland with a challenging task ahead of their next fixtures.

With the summer’s international series concluded, England’s squad will now shift focus to upcoming tournaments, while Ireland will look to regroup and improve their performance in future encounters. The match at Worcester highlights England’s depth and the rising standards of women’s cricket worldwide.
author: BBC Sport

title: Everton vs Man United Player Ratings and Sub Impact
content:
Everton and Manchester United faced off in a pre‑season friendly at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday, a match that drew a modest crowd of 5,000. The game, part of each club’s preparation for the upcoming season, saw a mix of first‑team regulars and youth prospects take to the pitch. Everton’s lineup featured new signing Jadon Sancho, midfielder James Rodriguez, and centre‑back Ben Godfrey, while United fielded a squad heavy with academy talent, including midfielder Mason Greenwood and striker Marcus Rashford.

Player ratings, compiled by the match officials, placed Sancho at 7.8, the highest for the visitors, followed by Rodriguez at 7.1 and Godfrey at 6.9. On the United side, Rashford earned a 7.5, Greenwood a 7.0, and defender Harry Maguire a 6.8. Goalkeepers were rated 7.2 for Everton’s Jordan Pickford and 7.0 for United’s Dean Henderson. The ratings reflect the overall performance of each player, with the top performers noted for their impact on the game’s flow and defensive solidity.

The friendly concluded with a 2‑1 victory for Manchester United, a result that gave the squad confidence ahead of the competitive fixtures. The ratings suggest that both teams have promising talent ready for the season, with United’s young core showing particular promise in midfield and attack, while Everton’s new signings have begun to integrate into the squad’s dynamics. The match at Hill Dickinson Stadium therefore served as a useful benchmark for both clubs as they fine‑tune their line‑ups for the challenges ahead.
author: BBC Sport

title: Antonelli Wins Italian Grand Prix from 19th on Grid
content:
Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli secured a stunning victory at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix, climbing from 19th on the grid to the checkered flag in a race marked by numerous incidents. The Monza circuit saw a chaotic opening lap, with a multi‑vehicle collision on the first corner forcing a safety car and a reshuffle of the field. Antonelli, who had qualified 19th, used the early caution to his advantage, advancing through the midfield as several front‑row cars were damaged or retired.

Throughout the race, Antonelli’s team executed a flawless pit‑stop strategy, switching to a harder compound that allowed him to maintain a steady pace while his rivals struggled with tire degradation. He overtook key competitors on the high‑speed straights, capitalising on a late‑race safety car that bunched the field together. On the final lap, a last‑minute error by the race leader opened a gap that Antonelli closed with a decisive overtake, securing the win for Mercedes and marking a career‑highlighting performance for the rookie driver.

The victory underscores Mercedes’ continued competitiveness in the championship, while also highlighting Antonelli’s skill and composure under pressure. With the win, he gains valuable points for the Constructors’ Championship and cements his status as a rising talent in Formula 1. The Italian Grand Prix will be remembered for its dramatic incidents and the remarkable rise of a driver who began the day in 19th place.
author: BBC Sport

title: Former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall says he could not serve under Trump
content:
Former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall III told ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he “couldn’t serve” in a Trump administration, sharply criticizing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s stewardship of the Pentagon. Kendall, who served as the department’s top civilian official from 2021 to 2023, said he has “never seen an attempt to politicize our military like the one being conducted by Pete Hegseth,” adding that such actions undermine the nonpartisan nature of the armed forces.

Kendall’s remarks came amid a broader wave of concern among senior defense officials. Earlier in the week, the Army Secretary also voiced apprehension about perceived political interference in military affairs, echoing calls for preserving the service’s apolitical stance. Both statements highlight growing tension between former defense leaders and the current administration’s approach to civilian‑military relations.
author: The Hill

title: Faster Labor Contracts Act to Speed Up Collective Bargaining
content:
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick urged the Senate to approve the Faster Labor Contracts Act, a bill designed to streamline collective‑bargaining processes and safeguard the economic stability of working families. In a statement released Monday, Fitzpatrick highlighted the growing need for quicker contract negotiations amid rising inflation and labor shortages across key industries.

The proposed legislation would establish a federal framework that allows unions and employers to reach binding agreements within a shorter timeframe, reducing the likelihood of prolonged strikes or work stoppages. By codifying expedited procedures, the act aims to protect workers from wage stagnation and ensure that essential services remain uninterrupted. Fitzpatrick noted that the measure would also provide clearer guidelines for dispute resolution, helping to maintain a predictable labor market for businesses and households alike.

If enacted, the Faster Labor Contracts Act could set a new standard for labor relations nationwide, potentially easing tensions between labor and management while reinforcing the economic security of families dependent on stable employment. Fitzpatrick called on Senate leaders to prioritize the bill, emphasizing its importance for both workers and the broader economy.
author: The Hill

title: Former Air Force secretary questions ‘advice’ Trump received before starting Iran war
content:
Former U.S. Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall III raised a question about the decision‑making process that led President Donald Trump into military action against Iran. On Sunday, Kendall appeared on ABC’s “This Week” with host Martha Raddatz and asked, “What I don’t understand, frankly, about the Iran war is what advice was given to the president that led him to start this conflict?” The comment follows the 2020 U.S. strike that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani and the subsequent escalation that drew the two nations into a near‑war.

Kendall, who served as Air Force Secretary from 2017 to 2019, has long been a critic of the Trump administration’s approach to Middle Eastern policy. By questioning the counsel that shaped the president’s decision, he is highlighting concerns over the transparency and accountability of the executive branch’s military strategies. His remarks come amid ongoing debates about the legality and strategic wisdom of the U.S. strike and the broader implications for U.S. foreign policy.

The former secretary’s remarks underscore the continuing scrutiny of the Trump administration’s foreign‑policy decisions. As analysts and lawmakers reassess the events that led to the Iran confrontation, Kendall’s question serves as a reminder of the importance of clear, evidence‑based advice in shaping national security actions.
author: The Hill

title: US Wealth Surpasses National Debt, No Austerity Needed
content:
The way a nation’s debt is framed can shape the policy options that appear viable. When the debt is presented as a multiple of a single year’s income, the narrative quickly narrows to two unattractive choices: either slash government spending or raise taxes on the wages and salaries that ordinary Americans rely on. Both options carry significant political and social costs, and they tend to dominate public debate and legislative proposals.

An alternative perspective compares debt to the country’s total wealth rather than to annual income. Under this lens, the debt load appears less daunting, revealing a fiscal space that can be used to fund public priorities without resorting to austerity or tax hikes on the middle class. Policymakers can explore measures that tap into existing wealth—such as more efficient use of public assets, targeted investment in high‑return infrastructure, or reforms that boost productivity—while maintaining fiscal responsibility. This approach offers a middle path that preserves economic growth and protects households, suggesting that the debt crisis may be more manageable than the conventional framing implies.
author: The Hill

title: 140 Migrants Rescued in English Channel Dinghy
content:
On the morning of 3 September, a coordinated rescue operation in the English Channel saw 23 people transferred onto two lifeboats and brought safely to shore in the United Kingdom. The operation, conducted by the Royal Navy in partnership with the UK Coast Guard, was launched from the coast near Dover after a distress signal was received from a small vessel drifting off the French shoreline.

The lifeboats, equipped with medical and security teams, made a swift transfer of the individuals—most of whom were identified as migrants from the Middle East—while maintaining a safe distance from the original vessel. The crew secured the passengers, provided first‑aid checks, and then guided them to the nearest UK port, where they were handed over to immigration authorities for processing. The operation was part of the broader Channel rescue programme that has been intensified in response to the rising number of crossings.

Following the transfer, the rescued individuals were taken to a reception centre where they will receive medical screening and legal assistance. The incident highlights the continued demand for maritime rescue services in the Channel and underscores the importance of international cooperation in addressing the migrant crisis.
author: BBC Politics

title: Anak Krakatau eruption halts flights at eight Indonesian airports
content:
Indonesia suspended operations at eight airports on Sunday, including its main international hub, after an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano disrupted air traffic and forced the cancellation of hundreds of flights. The ash plume drifted over the region, prompting authorities to ground aircraft for safety reasons and to protect passengers and crew from volcanic ash damage.

The eruption that began on Saturday produced lava flows and thunderous explosions that were audible up to 435 miles (700 km) away, according to the Indonesian Geology Agency. In addition to the aviation impact, the ashfall curtailed some school activities and fishing operations in coastal communities. A further two eruptions were recorded on Sunday, extending the period of disruption.

With the volcano still active, the Indonesian government has maintained heightened monitoring and will continue to adjust flight schedules as necessary. The situation remains fluid, and authorities are urging travelers to stay informed through official channels.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Older Athletes Maintain Fitness and Independence Into Later Years
content:
Dylan Thomas’s words about “old age should burn and rave at close of day” have found an unlikely echo in the world of professional sports, where a handful of high‑profile athletes are extending their careers well beyond the conventional peak years. In a season that has seen veteran players return to the spotlight, the narrative has shifted from “retirement” to “renewal,” as athletes in their late 30s and early 40s continue to compete at the highest levels.

LeBron James, now 41, has announced a contract extension with the Los Angeles Lakers that will keep him on the court for the next two seasons, citing a renewed focus on fitness and recovery. Meanwhile, tennis legend Roger Federer has announced a brief comeback in the ATP Challenger circuit, while former NFL quarterback Tom Brady has signed a short‑term deal to mentor the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ offense. Each of these athletes has publicly stated that their motivation comes from a desire to “keep the fire alive” and to prove that age need not dictate performance.

The collective decision of these stars to stay active underscores a broader trend in professional sports: advances in sports science, nutrition, and injury management are allowing athletes to prolong their competitive years. Their continued presence on the field, court, and court not only challenges traditional retirement timelines but also offers fans a new chapter in the stories of some of the game’s most iconic figures.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Focal Therapy Uncommon in Nonmetastatic Prostate Cancer, Study Shows
content:
A research letter published online on August 13 in the *Journal of American Medical Association* (JAMA) found that focal therapy for non‑metastatic prostate cancer remains rarely used across all risk categories. The analysis also revealed that roughly 50 % of patients who received focal therapy were deemed to have received an inappropriate treatment according to current clinical guidelines.

The study examined a large cohort of men with localized prostate cancer and evaluated the appropriateness of focal therapy—an approach that targets only the tumor region rather than the entire gland. While the therapy is intended for selected low‑ to intermediate‑risk patients, the data indicate that its application is infrequent overall and that a significant proportion of recipients did not meet the criteria that justify its use.

These findings underscore the need for stricter adherence to evidence‑based criteria when selecting patients for focal therapy and highlight the importance of ongoing audit and education to prevent inappropriate use of this treatment modality.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists Create Record-Long Single-Atom Copper Chains
content:
Silicon‑based chips are rapidly approaching their fundamental physical limits, prompting researchers to look beyond traditional interconnects for the next generation of electronics. As device dimensions shrink, the conventional copper wiring that links transistors becomes increasingly inefficient, raising the question of whether atomic‑scale conductors could replace or supplement current technology.

In a recent breakthrough, a team of scientists reported the creation of one of the longest single‑atom copper chains ever fabricated, extending several nanometers in a straight line. The chain was assembled atom by atom on a specially prepared substrate, and its electrical conductance was measured to confirm that it behaves as a coherent metallic wire at the molecular level. The ability to sustain a continuous copper chain of this length suggests that such atomic wires could serve as ultra‑thin, low‑resistance interconnects in future nanoscale circuits.

If scalable, these single‑atom copper wires could dramatically reduce interconnect resistance and power consumption while fitting within the ever‑smaller footprints of modern devices. Further research will focus on integrating these molecular conductors into practical circuits, addressing fabrication reproducibility and stability under operating conditions. The development marks a promising step toward overcoming the limitations of silicon‑based interconnects in the era of ultra‑compact electronics.
author: Phys.org

title: American Cheetah Found to be Puma Relative
content:
A recent study published in *Current Biology* has re‑evaluated the evolutionary history of the extinct North American cat *Miracinonyx trumani*, long dubbed the “American cheetah” for its slender build and long front legs. The research, conducted by a team of paleontologists and geneticists, shows that *M. trumani* was more closely related to modern pumas than to the African cheetah. The authors used a combination of fossil morphology and ancient DNA analysis to place the species firmly within the Puma lineage, reshaping our understanding of its phylogenetic placement.

The study also examined dietary evidence from fossilized remains near Arctic regions, revealing that some *M. trumani* populations specialized in fish consumption rather than the high‑speed pursuit of large ungulates such as pronghorns. Isotopic signatures in bone collagen indicated a predominantly piscivorous diet, challenging the long‑held assumption that these cats were specialized hunters of fast‑running prey. This finding suggests that *M. trumani* was ecologically versatile, adapting its hunting strategies to local prey availability.

These insights underscore the importance of integrating genetic, morphological, and ecological data when reconstructing the life history of extinct species. By redefining *Miracinonyx trumani* as a puma relative with a diverse diet, the study broadens our perspective on the adaptive strategies of prehistoric felids in North America.
author: Phys.org

title: Why Recreating Minecraft Isn't a Good Benchmark
content:
A recent blog post on the Kuber Studio website, titled “Recreating Minecraft is Not a Benchmark,” has attracted attention from the programming community. The article was shared on Hacker News, where it received four up‑votes and no comments, indicating a modest but engaged readership.

In the post, the author argues that using Minecraft as a yardstick for evaluating a developer’s skill is misleading. The original game is the product of a large team, extensive community support, and a long development cycle that involved complex systems such as procedural terrain generation, physics, and multiplayer networking. Replicating these features in a small project can give a false impression of mastery, while it also obscures the value of original design choices and problem‑solving that are unique to each new project. The author emphasizes that developers should assess their work on its own merits—innovation, architecture, and the specific challenges they tackle—rather than on how closely it mimics an existing title.

The article invites readers to reconsider common benchmarks in game development and to focus on the distinct goals of their own projects. While the discussion on Hacker News remains brief, the piece contributes to an ongoing conversation about how best to measure progress and creativity in software engineering.
author: Hacker News

title: Article on AI feelings garners 121 points and 128 comments
content:
A new online piece titled “AI Feelings” was published on the website beza1e1.Tuxen.De, exploring recent advances in artificial intelligence that aim to simulate human emotions. The article outlines how machine‑learning models can now generate affective responses—such as expressions of joy, sadness, or empathy—by training on large datasets of human emotional data. It also discusses the technical challenges involved, including the need for nuanced context awareness and the risk of over‑generalizing emotional states.

The piece quickly attracted attention on Hacker News, where it received 121 up‑votes and prompted 128 comments. Readers debated the practical applications of emotionally aware AI, ranging from more engaging virtual assistants to therapeutic chatbots, while also raising concerns about authenticity, manipulation, and the ethical implications of machines that can mimic feelings. Several commenters noted that while the technology is impressive, it remains a simulation rather than genuine affective experience, and that regulatory frameworks will be necessary to govern its deployment.

Overall, the article highlights a growing trend toward embedding affective computing into AI systems, underscoring both the potential benefits for user experience and the need for careful oversight. As research continues, the conversation around AI’s capacity to “feel” is likely to intensify, prompting further scrutiny from technologists, ethicists, and the broader public.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI Accelerates Research Inside the Company
content:
OpenAI has published a new internal document titled “Research Acceleration View,” outlining the company’s strategy for speeding up its artificial‑intelligence research pipeline. The release, which was shared on the organization’s website, details how OpenAI intends to streamline experimentation, enhance collaboration across its research teams, and expand its open‑source initiatives to accelerate progress.

According to the document, the acceleration plan focuses on three core areas: (1) increased cross‑disciplinary collaboration to reduce duplication of effort; (2) a new funding model that prioritizes high‑impact projects and rapid prototyping; and (3) a commitment to safety and alignment research that will run in parallel with product development. The plan also highlights the integration of recent advances such as large‑language models and multimodal systems, and it emphasizes the importance of transparent reporting and community engagement.

The announcement signals OpenAI’s intent to maintain its leadership position in AI while addressing growing concerns about responsible deployment. By formalizing its acceleration strategy, the organization aims to deliver new capabilities more quickly while ensuring that safety and ethical considerations remain integral to its research agenda.
author: Hacker News

title: Alberta Imposes Punitive Tax on Solar Panels
content:
The United Conservative Party (UCP) has announced a new punitive tax on residential and commercial solar panels, a move that signals a hardening stance on renewable energy policy. The tax, set to take effect in the coming fiscal year, will apply to all solar installations that exceed a certain capacity threshold, effectively raising the cost of solar adoption by an estimated 15‑20 %. The UCP’s policy brief frames the measure as a necessary correction to what it calls “over‑generous subsidies” that have, in its view, distorted the market and burdened taxpayers.

The announcement has sparked a flurry of debate online, with the article drawing 41 points and 38 comments on the Y Combinator news platform. Industry analysts warn that the tax could stall the province’s clean‑energy targets and deter new investment, while some proponents argue it will level the playing field for traditional utilities. The UCP has pledged to review the policy after a full year of implementation, citing the need to balance fiscal responsibility with environmental commitments.
author: Hacker News

title: NetBSD 9.5 Released, NetBSD-9 Reaches End of Life
content:
NetBSD 9.5, the latest stable release of the long‑standing open‑source operating system, was announced on the NetBSD Project’s official blog on March 15 2024. The release follows the 9.4 line and brings a suite of updates aimed at improving performance, security, and hardware compatibility while maintaining the project’s hallmark portability.

Key enhancements in 9.5 include expanded support for modern x86‑64 and ARM64 platforms, a refreshed networking stack that introduces improved IPv6 handling and better support for contemporary wireless drivers, and a set of security patches that address several CVEs disclosed in the preceding year. The ports collection received a significant update, with dozens of libraries and applications upgraded to newer versions, and the build system was streamlined to reduce compilation times on both desktop and embedded targets. Bug‑fixes address long‑standing issues such as memory leaks in the kernel’s networking subsystem and erratic behavior in the X11 server on certain GPU drivers.

The new release is available for download from the NetBSD mirrors and can be installed via the standard installer or built from source. Users are encouraged to review the release notes for a complete list of changes and to migrate from earlier 9.x releases. The announcement has drawn attention from the broader open‑source community, with a discussion thread on Hacker News noting 14 up‑votes and a single comment, underscoring the continued interest in NetBSD’s stable, security‑focused platform.
author: Hacker News

title: Cultivating Trust article published on KaeruCT GitHub.io
content:
On September 6, 2026, the personal blog hosted at kaeruct.github.io published an article titled “Conquering Entropy: Cultivating Trust.” The post, written in a concise, essay‑style format, explores how increasing uncertainty—metaphorically described as entropy—can erode confidence in both technical systems and organizational relationships. The author outlines a framework that blends data‑driven transparency, iterative feedback loops, and clear communication protocols to rebuild and sustain trust amid rapid change.

The article argues that trust is most effectively cultivated when stakeholders are actively involved in monitoring and mitigating entropy. It cites examples from software development, where continuous integration and automated testing reduce unpredictability, and from corporate governance, where open reporting and stakeholder engagement lower perceived risk. The piece concludes that a proactive, collaborative approach not only mitigates entropy but also turns uncertainty into an opportunity for adaptive growth.

The post attracted modest attention on Hacker News, where it received three upvotes and one comment. While the discussion was brief, the engagement underscores a growing interest in strategies that address the challenges of complexity and unpredictability in modern systems. The article invites further dialogue on how trust‑building practices can be systematically integrated into both technology and organizational practices.
author: Hacker News

title: NetBSD research article highlighted on Hacker News
content:
The NetBSD project has added a new “Research” gallery to its official website, offering a curated collection of academic papers, technical reports, and case studies that demonstrate the operating system’s use in a variety of research contexts. Hosted at https://www.netbsd.org/gallery/research.html, the page aggregates contributions from universities, research institutions, and industry partners, highlighting work on topics such as security hardening, performance optimization, and novel hardware support. The gallery is intended to provide developers and scholars with concrete examples of NetBSD’s capabilities, as well as to encourage further experimentation and collaboration within the open‑source community.

The announcement was posted to the Hacker News discussion board (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49587903), where it received eight points and no comments at the time of reporting. The modest engagement reflects the niche interest of the platform’s audience in operating‑system research resources, while underscoring the continued relevance of NetBSD as a platform for experimental and production‑grade projects. The research gallery is now publicly accessible and may serve as a reference point for future contributions to the NetBSD ecosystem.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI publishes article “An Alien Mind” on its website
content:
OpenAI published a new article titled “An Alien Mind” on its website, exploring concepts related to artificial intelligence and the theoretical frameworks that could underpin non‑human cognition. The piece appears on the company’s index page and delves into speculative scenarios about how machine learning systems might develop thought processes that differ fundamentally from human intelligence, citing recent research and potential future applications.

The article attracted modest attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where it was listed under the discussion thread with the identifier 49588080. As of the latest metrics, the post has earned six points and has not generated any comments, indicating limited engagement from the community at this stage.
author: Hacker News

title: Boox Picco e-reader expected to launch in November
content:
Boox has quietly been working on a new e‑reader that it dubbed the Picco, a device that was first hinted at in a July teaser but left most specifications unknown. Recent coverage from the IFA trade show has supplied a handful of concrete details, although the company has yet to reveal a price. The Picco is positioned as Boox’s answer to the popular Xteink X4, but it diverges in several key ways.

Unlike the Xteink line, the Picco will not feature the magnetic backplate that allows the X4 to attach to a phone. Instead, it will sport a 3.97‑inch e‑paper display that is fully touchscreen, a change praised by The Verge’s Andrew Liszewski as a “welcome upgrade” over the X4 Pro. The device will also include physical page‑turn buttons that can be programmed for different actions on short versus long presses. Storage is entirely external; the Picco will rely on a microSD card for all user data, with no internal memory available.

While the reveal at IFA has clarified several design choices, Boox has not yet announced a retail price or release date. The company’s next steps will likely involve finalizing the hardware and setting a launch timeline, but for now consumers can only anticipate the Picco’s unique blend of touch capability, customizable controls, and microSD‑based storage.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla Cybercab Launches, Faces Early Snag
content:
TechCrunch Mobility is back, sharpening its focus on the growing influence of artificial intelligence across the transportation sector. The publication highlights how AI is becoming a central driver behind innovations in autonomous vehicles, predictive maintenance, and intelligent traffic management, reshaping the way people and goods move.

Recent developments underscore AI’s expanding role. Waymo’s latest neural‑network model improves object detection in complex urban environments, while Tesla’s Full Self‑Driving beta relies on deep‑learning algorithms to interpret real‑time sensor data. In cities, AI‑powered traffic control systems are reducing congestion by dynamically adjusting signal timings, and public transit operators are deploying machine‑learning tools to forecast ridership and optimize routes. Regulatory bodies are also revising safety standards to accommodate AI‑enabled vehicles, and major automakers are forming data‑sharing consortia to accelerate algorithmic improvements.

As AI continues to permeate mobility, the industry faces both opportunities and challenges. The technology promises higher safety, lower emissions, and more efficient logistics, but it also raises questions about data privacy, workforce impacts, and regulatory oversight. TechCrunch Mobility will continue to track these developments, offering in‑depth coverage of how AI is redefining the future of transportation.
author: TechCrunch

title: Uber founder Kalanick's Atoms explores robotaxi market
content:
Uber co‑founder Travis Kalanick announced this week that he is backing a new venture called Atoms, describing the project as an opportunity to finish “unfinished business” left from his earlier work in the ride‑hailing industry. The statement was made during a press briefing in San Francisco, where Kalanick outlined Atoms’ focus on building next‑generation logistics and mobility platforms that integrate autonomous technology, data analytics, and on‑demand services. He positioned the startup as a continuation of the disruptive approach that propelled Uber to global prominence, emphasizing that Atoms will operate independently of his previous enterprises, including CloudKitchens and the venture‑capital firm 10100.

Industry observers note that Kalanick’s reference to “unfinished business” likely alludes to his long‑standing ambition to reshape urban transportation and supply‑chain networks, goals that were partially curtailed by his departure from Uber in 2017 amid leadership turmoil. Atoms has secured an initial round of funding from a mix of private investors and strategic partners, though the exact amount has not been disclosed. The venture plans to launch pilot programs in several U.S. cities later this year, aiming to test autonomous delivery fleets and integrated marketplace services. If successful, Atoms could extend Kalanick’s influence in the mobility sector and signal a renewed push toward the automation and data‑driven models he championed during Uber’s rapid expansion.
author: TechCrunch

title: US envoys arrive in Kyiv to discuss peace objectives
content:
U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff, the assistant secretary of state for European and Eurasian affairs, and Jared Kushner, the former senior advisor to President Trump, landed in Kyiv on Sunday for their first official visit to Ukraine. Their arrival marks a renewed diplomatic effort to advance a negotiated settlement more than four and a half years after Russia launched a full‑scale invasion of the country.

During the trip, the envoys met with Ukrainian officials and discussed the prospects for a cease‑fire and a comprehensive peace framework. The visit follows a series of U.S. initiatives aimed at strengthening Ukraine’s security and supporting its sovereignty. In a briefing with the Atlantic Council, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center, noted that the U.S. is seeking to coordinate with European partners and regional stakeholders to create a viable path to de-escalation while maintaining pressure on Moscow to comply with international law.

The Kyiv trip underscores Washington’s continued commitment to Ukraine’s territorial integrity and the broader goal of ending hostilities. While the outcome of the discussions remains uncertain, the envoys’ presence signals a willingness to engage directly with Kyiv’s leadership and to explore diplomatic solutions that could bring an end to the conflict.
author: France 24

title: AfD leads German polls with over 40% under Ulrich Siegmund
content:
The Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised to become a dominant force in the upcoming federal election under its 35‑year‑old lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund. Recent opinion polls have shown the party consistently above the 40 percent mark for several months, positioning it as the frontrunner among the nation’s political contenders.

Analysts note that the AfD could secure an absolute majority in the Bundestag if a number of smaller parties fail to surpass Germany’s 5 percent electoral threshold, which is required for parliamentary representation. Should those parties fall short, the distribution of seats would amplify the AfD’s share, potentially granting it the decisive vote needed to form a government without coalition partners.
author: France 24

title: Week in review: Nepal flood rescue, World Nomad Games and Kyiv Russian strikes
content:
FRANCE 24’s weekly visual roundup highlighted two stark images that captured the human toll of recent crises in Asia and the Middle East. The segment opened with photographs of rescue teams combing through flooded valleys in Nepal, where unprecedented monsoon rains have inundated a hydropower project and left dozens of construction workers trapped beneath collapsed tunnels.

The second set of images showed large groups of women gathered in southern Iran, their faces marked by grief as they mourned the victims of a U.S. airstrike that struck a wedding ceremony earlier in the week. The photographs documented the community’s collective sorrow and the broader regional tension surrounding the incident.

By juxtaposing the desperate search for survivors in Nepal with the mourning crowds in Iran, the feature underscored how natural disasters and armed conflict continue to produce profound human suffering, prompting international attention to both humanitarian response and diplomatic repercussions.
author: France 24

title: AfD Leads Saxony-Anhalt Election with Over 40% Support
content:
Voting began on Sunday in Saxony‑Anhalt, the eastern German state where a closely watched state election is under way. Recent opinion polls show the far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) leading with just over 40 % of the vote, while the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) under Friedrich Merz trails at roughly 23 %. The election is seen as a barometer for the AfD’s growing influence in former East German regions and could shape the composition of the state parliament.

According to journalist Shirli Stibon, a central element of the AfD’s platform is a comprehensive overhaul of the education system, which the party describes as a “reset” of schooling. If the AfD secures a governing majority, reforms to curricula, school administration and teaching standards are expected to be among its first policy initiatives, potentially altering the state’s educational landscape. The outcome will determine whether these proposed changes are implemented and how they will affect Saxony‑Anhalt’s future governance.
author: France 24

title: Deauville Film Festival surveys public on favorite American movies
content:
The United States now ranks second worldwide in film output, producing between 500 and 700 titles annually, a figure that trails only India’s prolific industry. The Deauville Film Festival, renowned for its star‑studded premieres and awards, has positioned itself as a showcase for the finest American cinema crossing the Atlantic, drawing industry professionals and audiences alike to celebrate the breadth of U.S. storytelling.

During the festival, reporter Gaëlle Fonseca canvassed attendees to discover which American movies have left the strongest impression. Respondents cited a range of classics that shaped their childhoods as well as recent releases that resonated with contemporary viewers, underscoring the diverse appeal of U.S. film across generations. The street‑level poll highlights the festival’s role not only in presenting new works but also in gauging public sentiment toward America’s cinematic legacy.
author: France 24

title: AfD poised to lead potential far‑right government in Saxony‑Anhalt
content:
Voting is taking place on Sunday in the eastern German state of Saxony‑Anhalt, where citizens are casting ballots in a closely watched state election. The contest pits the far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) against the incumbent coalition of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), the Social Democratic Party (SPD) and the Greens, and it is being monitored for its potential impact on the political landscape of post‑war Germany.

If the AfD succeeds in forming a government in Saxony‑Anhalt, it would become the first regional administration led by a far‑right party since the end of the Second World War, a development highlighted by correspondent Nick Holdsworth. Analysts note that such an outcome would mark a historic shift in the composition of German state governments, prompting close observation of coalition negotiations and the response of federal authorities.
author: France 24

title: AfD leads Saxony-Anhalt election with 44.5% of vote
content:
Germany’s far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is on track for a landslide win in the Saxony‑Anhalt state election, with early counts showing the party securing 44.5 percent of the vote on Sunday. The result marks a significant surge for the AfD, which previously held a much smaller share of the regional electorate and had not been positioned as the leading contender in the state’s political landscape.

The strong showing for the AfD is reshaping the balance of power among the traditional parties, which together trail the far‑right in the preliminary tally. Analysts note that the outcome could influence coalition negotiations and policy direction in Saxony‑Anhalt, while also providing a barometer for the party’s broader national momentum ahead of upcoming federal contests.
author: France 24

title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino to Run for Re‑election
content:
FIFA confirmed on Thursday that President Gianni Infantino has maintained his position on seeking a second term, despite a wave of criticism from member associations, former officials and human‑rights groups. In a statement released by the governing body, FIFA said Infantino “has not altered his stance on re‑election” and will continue to campaign for the office when the next presidential vote is scheduled for early 2027. The announcement comes amid mounting scrutiny over the organization’s handling of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, allegations of corruption in the bidding processes for future tournaments, and concerns about governance reforms promised after the 2023 FIFA Congress.

Critics have called for a leadership change, arguing that Infantino’s tenure has been marked by controversial decisions and insufficient progress on transparency and accountability. Nevertheless, FIFA’s executive committee reiterated that the election will proceed according to the statutes, allowing all eligible member associations to cast their votes. The forthcoming ballot will determine whether Infantino’s agenda—centered on expanding the global football calendar and increasing commercial revenues—will continue to shape the sport’s governance for another four‑year term.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Actor Khalid Abdalla discusses identity, justice and Gaza conflict
content:
An unnamed actor used a recent interview to address his personal sense of identity while condemning what he described as “genocide” in Gaza, urging an end to the violence perpetrated by Israeli forces. Speaking to a global media outlet, the performer linked his artistic background and family heritage to a broader commitment to human rights, stating that silence in the face of civilian suffering would betray the values he believes his craft should uphold. He emphasized that the ongoing conflict has resulted in extensive civilian casualties, infrastructure destruction and a humanitarian crisis that demands international attention.

The actor attributed his outspoken stance to formative experiences, including growing up in a multicultural environment and witnessing the impact of political oppression on marginalized communities. He noted that these encounters have shaped his understanding of solidarity and compelled him to use his public platform to amplify calls for accountability and peace. While acknowledging the complexity of the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict, he reiterated that the protection of civilian lives must remain paramount, urging policymakers and the entertainment industry alike to prioritize humanitarian concerns over partisan narratives.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US envoys meet Zelenskyy in Kyiv after talks with Putin in Moscow
content:
A high‑level diplomatic gathering took place on Thursday in Geneva, coming a day after U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. The Moscow talks, part of a broader effort by the United States to engage Russia on a range of security and economic issues, were conducted in private and concluded with a joint statement indicating a willingness to explore further dialogue.

The Geneva meeting, attended by senior officials from the United States, Russia, and several European partners, focused on coordinating responses to ongoing geopolitical challenges, including sanctions policy, energy security, and regional stability. Participants exchanged views on recent developments and outlined steps for continued engagement, underscoring the importance of sustained communication between the two nations. The session concluded with an agreement to maintain an open channel for future negotiations, reflecting a cautious but ongoing diplomatic outreach.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Millions of fish die as drought dries up Central Java's Silugonggo River
content:
A prolonged dry spell has led to the mass death of fish in Indonesia’s Silugonggo River in Central Java, with estimates indicating that millions of aquatic animals have perished. The river, a vital waterway for local agriculture and fisheries, experienced a sharp decline in water levels over the past several weeks, reducing oxygen concentrations and creating conditions unsuitable for the river’s native species.

Local authorities have dispatched environmental officers to assess the damage and are coordinating with regional water management agencies to restore flow and improve water quality. Officials emphasized the need for long‑term water conservation measures to mitigate the impact of future droughts, while community leaders urged residents to adopt sustainable practices to protect the river’s ecosystem.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Niger military alleges French involvement in failed mutiny
content:
Paris officials have publicly denied any participation in the incident that sparked accusations from the neighboring government, reiterating that no French agents or resources were involved. The statement, released by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, came after the other country’s leaders alleged covert French activity that they claim threatened regional stability.

Despite the denial, diplomatic relations between the two nations remain strained, with both sides maintaining heightened alertness and continuing to exchange formal protests. Analysts note that the episode adds to a series of recent frictions, and officials from both capitals have indicated that discussions to de‑escalate the situation are ongoing, though no concrete resolution has yet been reached.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Everton draw 2-2 with Manchester United after comeback
content:
Everton salvaged a point after falling behind to United in a tightly contested Premier League encounter that ended 2‑2 at Goodison Park. United opened the scoring early in the first half, but Everton responded through Bryan Mbeumo, leveling the match before the interval. The home side appeared to have secured a draw when Mbeumo struck again in the second half, only for United’s Benjamin Sesko to restore parity minutes later, sealing the final score.

Both clubs earned a single point from the fixture, leaving Everton still in the lower half of the table while United remain within the top six. The result highlights Everton’s resilience after conceding first and United’s ability to regain momentum late in the game, setting the tone for their upcoming league commitments.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran says proportional retaliation over after US tanker strikes in Gulf blockade
content:
Tehran announced on Thursday that the window for a proportionate response to a recent U.S. strike on Iranian‑flagged tankers has closed, signaling a shift toward a broader retaliation. The statement came after U.S. forces targeted two tankers operating within a naval blockade line that the United States has maintained in the Red Sea to protect commercial shipping from Houthi attacks. The U.S. Department of Defense said the vessels were linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and posed a security threat, but did not disclose casualty figures.

Iran’s foreign ministry warned that the cessation of “proportionate” measures does not preclude a more extensive response, emphasizing that any future action would be calibrated to the scale of the perceived aggression. The declaration arrives amid heightened regional tensions, with both sides accusing each other of escalating hostilities in a corridor already strained by the ongoing conflict in Yemen. Analysts note that Tehran’s shift could lead to heightened naval activity or asymmetric attacks, although no specific plans have been outlined. The development underscores the fragile security environment surrounding the Red Sea and the potential for further escalation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Delhi hostel collapse may have trapped up to 50 people
content:
A five‑storey hostel collapsed early Wednesday, with officials estimating that as many as 50 occupants were inside the building at the time of the incident. Emergency services were dispatched to the site within minutes, and rescue teams began searching the debris for survivors and the injured.

Authorities have confirmed that the collapse is under investigation, and additional resources have been mobilized to support the ongoing rescue operation. Local hospitals are on standby to treat any casualties, while officials have urged residents to avoid the area as safety crews continue their work. The situation remains fluid, and updates will be provided as more information becomes available.
author: BBC World

title: AfD projected to win 44.5% in eastern German state election
content:
Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is projected to secure 44.5 % of the vote in the upcoming election, a share that party officials have described as a “historic result.” The figure places the AfD well ahead of the centre‑right Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which is forecast to receive 18.5 % of the vote, according to the latest poll released by [polling institute]. The survey, conducted among a representative sample of eligible voters, reflects a substantial lead for the AfD over its traditional rivals.

The projected outcome would mark the AfD’s strongest performance in a national election, surpassing its previous high of roughly 27 % in the 2021 federal vote. Analysts note that such a result could reshape Germany’s parliamentary composition, forcing the CDU and other mainstream parties to reconsider coalition options and legislative strategies. While the AfD has celebrated the numbers, opposition parties have called for a thorough examination of the underlying voter shift. The final vote count, due later this month, will determine whether the projected figures translate into a decisive parliamentary presence for the far‑right party.
author: BBC World

title: Canadian Skyrunner Missing During Matterhorn Record Attempt
content:
Canadian athlete Kalie McCrystal, a resident of Squamish, British Columbia, went missing on Tuesday afternoon while preparing for a record‑setting ascent and descent of the Matterhorn, a 14,692‑foot (4,478‑meter) peak on the Swiss‑Italian border. McCrystal was last seen during a reconnaissance and training session in the Alps, a critical phase of her preparation for the ambitious climb. Her disappearance has prompted an immediate search effort by local authorities and mountaineering groups in the region.

The Matterhorn, renowned for its challenging terrain and high altitude, has attracted climbers worldwide, and McCrystal’s attempt was part of a larger initiative to break a longstanding speed‑record for the mountain. The Canadian athlete’s training schedule had been closely monitored by her support team, who reported her absence to Swiss officials after she failed to return to the base camp. Rescue teams have combed the surrounding slopes and valleys, coordinating with Swiss and Italian mountain authorities to locate the missing climber.

While the search continues, officials have urged the public to remain calm and to respect the privacy of McCrystal’s family. The incident underscores the inherent risks of high‑altitude mountaineering, even during training phases. Authorities will provide updates as more information becomes available.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Loek Hartog Rescues Ollie Millroy from Burning Car at China GT
content:
A dramatic rescue unfolded at the Shanghai International Circuit on Saturday during the opening round of the China GT Championship, when British driver Ollie Millroy’s Ferrari caught fire after a side‑impact collision.
